p: The National Stone Centre sits right beside the High Peak Trail, which follows the route of the old Cromford and High Peak Railway, one of the earliest railways in the country. Today it's a traffic-free path for walkers and cyclists, and from the centre you can follow it to Black Rocks, a gritstone outcrop with sweeping views over the Derwent Valley. It's a popular spot with climbers, so you may well see people scaling the crags.

Back in Wirksworth, the Ecclesbourne Valley Railway runs heritage trains down the valley towards Duffield, a gentle way to see the countryside without the car. If you visit in late spring, keep an eye out for Wirksworth's well dressings, a Derbyshire tradition where wells are decorated with intricate pictures made from petals and other natural materials. They're beautiful and only on display for a short time.
Carsington Water, a large reservoir a few miles away, adds walking, cycling and watersports to the mix, so it's easy to turn a visit into a full weekend.

A quick note on fossils: the quarry faces here are protected, so admire them rather than chipping away. Keen collectors are far better off visiting the shop, where you can take home a proper souvenir without harming the site.
